title: Online co-op is now in the Portal Beasts demo! Here’s what I’ve been building with AI
author: PortalBeasts
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’m working on **Portal Beasts**, a creature-collecting RPG where you explore different worlds, catch beasts, build your team, and fight alongside them in real-time combat.

I’ve now added **two-player online co-op**, with its own campaign. You can explore together, battle wild beasts, and build your own teams. The video shows some of it in action!

Since this is an AI game dev community, here’s where AI fits into my workflow:

* **Coding and debugging:** AI helps me implement features, investigate bugs, and build tests.
* **Pixel art:** I use PixelLab for parts of the creature and environment artwork, including directional sprites and animations.
* **Iteration:** There’s a lot of checking and correcting results—keeping a creature’s design consistent across eight directions has been a challenge of its own!

The game is built in **Godot**, with Aseprite also used in the art workflow.

**Co-op is still in beta, so expect bugs and rough edges.** I’ve been testing with different PCs and connections, but connection stability, combat synchronization, and performance still need more real-world testing.

The demo is available on Steam. If you try it with a friend, I’d love to hear what felt fun, what was confusing, and what broke. Reports from the joining player are especially helpful.

Happy to answer questions about the game or the AI workflow!  
  
**Try the free demo on Steam:** [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4545580/Portal\_Beasts\_Demo/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4545580/Portal_Beasts_Demo/)

comments.author: Sasbe93
comments.body:
Klasse Lasse. Looks nice. I like the pokemon inspired world and the vibes. It seems performant, which is important.



Here is my negative (sorry) feedback:

A lot of the portal beasts looks very boring and like usual animals.

The tutorial should give us hints, when we need to use them and not one minute before. I can remember someone was telling me how to control the portal beast. I already forget it when I needed it for the first fight. Also I couldn't remember someone told me I have to use the mouse to fight lol.



But I would say the biggest issue for me are the controls. I don't know if there are any games out there who have this kind of controls but it feels very unusual for me. Its like a weird combo of pokemon rpg and moba. I had to switch to quick cast because to switch weapons before attacking while in combat is very odd.

Also why the right mouse click is doing nothing? That made me crazy. My right hand was completely underutilized, while my left hand felt like it had to do everything except aiming.

In normal casting mode, I would prefer attacks with left and right click and switch weapons with tab, so I can use the abilities faster. Or like in a moba, first click on the key, then using the mouse. And I would like to use the same key for switching between pet and human. Unfortunately, however, duplicate key assignments are not allowed. Also why I cant overwrite keys? I have first to go to the other control and picking a place holder key, so I can change the controls.



But if that's improved, it could turn out to be a fun game. I am a little excited.

replies.author: PortalBeasts
replies.body:
Thanks for taking the time to write all of this! And no need to apologise, I see this as constructive feedback. You’ve explained what felt confusing or frustrating and given specific examples and suggestions, which gives me something I can actually work with.

When you’ve spent so much time developing a game, it’s easy to take the controls and mechanics for granted. Hearing how they feel to someone playing for the first time helps me see where I need to do a better job, especially with tutorial timing, controls, and key rebinding.

That trainer interrupting your battle sounds particularly frustrating after you’d nearly won it. Thanks for pointing that out too.

I’m glad you still had some fun with it! I’ll go through your feedback carefully and work on improving the things you’ve highlighted.

replies.author: Sasbe93
replies.body:
I don't think i am exactly the target audience but yes, I had some fun. So personally I think it can work as a game.

  
Do you know what would be cool? If some abilities work different by terrain(like using a tree or you have to stand over grass or something like this).

Here are some more points I hope you can work with:

\-The go to A and then back to B missions were a little annoying and didn't feel right.

\-Left click to throw a limited catching device is not a good idea. I work on three screens and each time I switch to the game, I use left click to focus it and what is happening? The trainer throws instantly one of the catching balls and I have to got back to the town. In my opinion left click should do some usual stuff, but not rarely things.

\-Many attacks feel too similar. For example: What is the difference between bubbleshot and water slash? Both are water melee attacks with the same range and same cooldown(you don't notice the 0,5 seconds difference when spamming them). The beastdex tells me, one is special and one is physical, but that it all? And these are the basic attacks from three creatures: Blobble, Pladdle and Bubbler. Morde diversity would be cool.

\-The first times my creatures got a new ability, it was not that obvious for me that I had to choose an attack, that will be forgotten. I thought I had to upgrade an attack (because I am too stupid to read). A warning would be nice.

\-I never had to heal my creatures with potions, because it was too easy to level up and heal them this way. And if I had none left, I just had to go back to a hospital.

\-The game told me, I had to go to the vale. But I didn't found that anywhere. Was this the end of the demo?

  
A side note:

Before you make any major changes to the controls, you should get some feedback from others. Maybe I'm just being picky. For my part, I just thought that, if you can control the movements of the characters also with the mouse would be more comfortable(like a hack'n slay or a rts). But that probably wouldn't fit the game's theme, style and philosophy anymore.
